newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hyundai wins licence for Vietnam car plant.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai wins licence for Vietnam car plant.

text.p: South Korea's Hyundai Motor Co will be granted a licence to open a joint venture plant in Vietnam before the end of this year, a top official of the government's Foreign Investment Department said on Thursday.
General Director Vu Huy Hoang told Reuters approval for the roughly $250 million project with the Ministry of Interior would take the number of licences issued for foreign car makers to 15.
A Hyundai official in Hanoi, who declined to be named, said he had no information on when the project would get final approval.

Some car makers have complained that too many licences have been approved for a market which stood at just 39,800 units in 1995. But the government says it has no plans to limit the number of foreign joint ventures in the industry.
Vice Minister for Industry Nguyen Xuan Chuan said at an industry conference this week that vehicle demand would more than double to 80,800 units by 2005.

However, he said that if demand continued to outstrip government projections at its current rate, the annual market could stand at 105,000 unit by 2005. That would be equivalent to 77 percent of production capacity.

Chuan told Reuters at a foreign investment fair on Thursday that the industry ministry had been urging the government for the past two years to scrap import quotas for unassembled vehicles, which are known as complete knockdown kits (CKDs).
This year's car CKD import quota is 6,000, a tiny number which has to be shared between the half-dozen plants now operating with an estimated combined capacity of some 30,000 units a year.
Chuan said a decision on when to withdraw the import quota system was up to the prime minister and added that, in the meantime, another quota would be set for next year.
